title: Potato and Leek Soup (Potage Parmentier)
description: Potage Parmentier is a classic French Continental soup made with sweet leeks, floury potatoes, and rich stock, blended into a silky smooth purée and finished with cream. Elegant and comforting, it can be served hot as a refined starter or chilled as the classic Vichyssoise.

ingredients.title: For the Soup
items: Leeks (white and light green parts only), cleaned and thinly sliced – 500 g
Floury potatoes (Russet or Yukon Gold), peeled and diced – 600 g
Bouquet garni (thyme, parsley stems, bay leaf) – 1

ingredients.title: For Garnish
items: Extra virgin olive oil or truffle oil – a few drops

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Leeks
steps: Trim off the dark green tops of the leeks.
Slice the leeks lengthwise, wash thoroughly to remove any grit, and cut into thin half-moons.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Sweat the Aromatics
steps: Heat the butter and olive oil in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium-low heat.
Add the leeks and onion with a pinch of salt.
Cook gently for 8–10 minutes until softened without browning.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Cook the Soup
steps: Add the diced potatoes and crushed garlic (if using).
Pour in the hot stock and add the bouquet garni.
Bring to a gentle simmer, skim any foam, and cook for 20–25 minutes until the potatoes are completely tender.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Blend and Finish
steps: Remove and discard the bouquet garni.
Blend the soup until completely smooth using a high-speed blender or immersion blender.
Pass through a fine chinois or sieve for an ultra-silky texture.
Return to the saucepan and stir in the heavy cream.
Adjust the consistency if necessary and season with sea salt and white pepper.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Presentation
steps: Serve the soup hot in warm bowls.
Finish with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil or truffle oil.
Add a quenelle of crème fraîche, crispy leek julienne, or microgreens for an elegant restaurant-style presentation.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot with warm crusty sourdough or artisan bread.
Pair with Gruyère gougères or Parmesan crisps for a refined starter.
Serve chilled as Vichyssoise during summer, garnished with crème fraîche and fresh chives.

chefTips: Sweat the leeks gently without browning to preserve their delicate sweetness and pale colour.
Use homemade chicken or vegetable stock for the best depth of flavour.
Pass the blended soup through a fine chinois for a luxurious restaurant-quality texture.
Do not boil after adding the cream to maintain a smooth finish.
For an elegant variation, chill the soup and serve as Vichyssoise with crème fraîche and caviar.
